title: Reading literary fiction improves theory of mind.
central_claims: Brief literary-fiction reading temporarily improves theory-of-mind performance relative to nonfiction or popular fiction.

source_manifest.title: Camerer et al. SSRP supplementary methods and Tables 1, 3 and 4
source_manifest.finding: Literary fiction versus nonfiction failed in pooled SSRP: r=-.027, p=.468, N=714. A different independent replication of Experiment 5 reported support, but its synthesis found a small nonsignificant heterogeneous effect.

source_manifest.title: The Effect of Reading a Short Passage of Literary Fiction on Theory of Mind: A Replication of Kidd and Castano (2013)
source_manifest.finding: Independent Experiment 5 replication finds literary-fiction advantage under specified covariate/exclusion choices; a small meta-analysis is nonsignificant and heterogeneous.

answers.rationale: At least one independent replication reports a supportive literary-fiction effect under its specified analysis. Other well-powered tests are null and synthesis remains mixed, so this existential yes is not a consensus judgment.

research.summary: Literary fiction versus nonfiction failed in pooled SSRP: r=-.027, p=.468, N=714.
